results.title: [2504.10545] HSTU-BLaIR: Lightweight Contrastive Text Embedding for Generative Recommender

item.text: {"text":"Closest direct evidence: [HSTU-BLaIR (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.10545) augments HSTU with contrastive textual item embeddings and reports improvements over original HSTU and an OpenAI-embedding variant on its evaluated datasets. However, BLaIR uses pretraining on Amazon reviews and metadata, so those weights are excluded here; its results do not establish gains from scratch or on the fixed four-category benchmark. [Sequence-level Semantic Representation Fusion (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18166) also cautions that directly adding text and ID embeddings can be ineffective because their characteristics differ. Earlier [FDSA](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2019/600) supports learning feature transitions alongside item transitions, providing architectural motivation rather than evidence for this specific HSTU experiment.\n\nConstraint-compatible hypothesis: retain HSTU and jointly learn a small title/description encoder from random initialization—pooled token embeddings with a projection, or a shallow CNN preserving phrases and model identifiers. Gate its representation into the item ID embedding and use the same composite item representation for history inputs and candidate scoring, all within one trained network/checkpoint per category. Shared tokens could transfer interaction supervision to sparse items; phrase features might distinguish purpose and compatibility cues, but this remains unverified without pretrained semantics. Compare pooled tokens against phrase encoding and gated fusion under the fixed seeds, training limits, splits and four-category macro validation HR@10. Preserve numbers, units and model strings during tokenization; use only observed titles/descriptions. No retrieved evidence establishes superiority over lexical negative mining under this exact protocol."}
